dsg a1: Do the slabs STAND UPRIGHT, butted face to face and shoved hard against each other, locked up like the two cases behind them? — FAIL, and it is the exact error R-12 was written to fix. The slabs LIE FLAT, splayed open like an opened book - not upright, not butted face to face, not locked up. Two phones lying face-up on a plinth read as display stock, so the mirrored fight that 'and Apple fight over the phone market' needs is simply not depicted. This is the shot's entire payload.

dsg r1: Is the rest of the display held exactly as established in L17 - plate glass, black platform with its red scuffed arc, spotlight, case proportions? — FAIL. Essentially nothing carried: the plate-glass side panels became a wooden proscenium frame; the red scuffed arc became faint pink scratches; the spotlight cone changed shape and the platform gained a large cream light pool; the cases changed proportion and gained scuff marks they did not have. A delta frame's whole contract is that only the authored change moves.

dsg r2: Is the crowd of passers-by held - same people, in coats and headscarves with shopping bags? — FAIL, twice over. A wholly different set of people, drawn smaller with a different face treatment and repositioned from the flanks to a band across the top - a continuity break; AND they wear short-sleeved t-shirts, contemporary casual wear and modern hairstyles - an ERA break. The frame's costume no longer reads 1983.

dsg s1: Era register: warm outline, flat cel, chromatic; and is red used semantically only? — Outline and cel are correct (ink hue 12.3deg, R-B +27.2; median saturation 0.2706) - but the red accent lost its semantics. In L17 red is the contact arc, the punch element; here it survives only as scattered scratch marks with no single semantic referent, which the era suffix licenses red for.

The two phone slabs lie FLAT on the platform splayed open like a book instead of standing upright butted face to face and locked up, so the mirrored fight the line needs is not depicted; the held set was re-invented (plate-glass panels became a wooden proscenium, the red scuffed arc became faint scratches, the spotlight and platform lighting changed, the cases changed proportion); and the crowd is a different crowd in contemporary short-sleeved dress rather than L17's 1980s coats and headscarves, which is an era break as well as a continuity break.
